stories.headline: Lula da Silva wins fourth term as Brazil president after defeating Flávio Bolsonaro
stories.body:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won a fourth term as president of Brazil on Sunday [c1]. He defeated Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the election [c2]. Flávio Bolsonaro is the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro [c2]. This presidential win is unprecedented in Brazilian history [c1].

Lula da Silva previously served as president of Brazil between 2003 and 2011 [c5]. He was imprisoned from 2018 to 2019 on corruption charges [c4]. Those charges were later overturned [c4]. He is 80 years old [c12]. During the vote count in São Paulo, leftist federal lawmaker Erika Hilton spoke about Lula da Silva [c6]. She called him a statesman and a giant [c6].

Flávio Bolsonaro is 45 years old [c12]. He finished first in the first round of the presidential election [c3]. Former President Jair Bolsonaro led Lula da Silva by more than 2.2 million votes in that first round [c10]. Brazil has nearly 160 million registered voters [c11]. More than 33 million of those voters did not participate in the first round [c11].

Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin issued an order on election day [c9]. Voting was extended nationwide across Brazil by two hours after his order [c9]. In Salvador, a court in Bahia ordered the arrest of a top transportation official [c15]. The arrest order was based on allegations of reducing public buses on election day [c15].

When Reuters provided live coverage with over 78% of votes counted in the runoff, Lula da Silva led with 51.21% [c8]. Flávio Bolsonaro held 48.79% at that point [c8]. With nearly 99% of votes counted, Lula da Silva received 51.75% of the vote [c12]. Flávio Bolsonaro received 48.25% of the vote [c12].

Pro-Bolsonaro congressman Nikolas Ferreira spoke to journalists during the election [c13]. He said either they win or they win [c13]. He added that people had been warned [c13].

Former President Jair Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years in prison for plotting a coup [c14]. His political group remains powerful in parliament [c7]. Bolsonaro's Liberal Party and allied parties could control over 280 seats in Brazil's lower house [c7]. They could also control up to 50 seats in the Senate [c7].

vocab.meaning: never done or known before
kept in prison or captivity
cancelled or reversed a official decision
claims that someone has done something wrong

stories.headline: Israel prepares for general election with half a million new eligible voters
stories.body:
Half a million first-time voters are eligible to vote in Israel's general election [c16]. Around 70,000 Israelis are flying in from abroad to cast ballots [c16]. Arab citizens make up around one-fifth of Israel's population [c21].

Gadi Eisenkot leads the centrist Yashar party in Israel [c17]. He is a former military chief of staff [c17]. His son was killed during the Gaza War [c18]. A participant in a pro-Netanyahu TV debate used a racist slur against Eisenkot [c19]. The participant referred to him as a Moroccan monkey [c19]. Eisenkot and other opposition party leaders ruled out forming a coalition government with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu [c26].

US President Donald Trump publicly endorsed Benjamin Netanyahu for Prime Minister of Israel [c24]. A survey shows that over 70% of Jewish Israelis support establishing a state commission of inquiry into the October 7, 2023 attacks [c20].

Billionaire American investor Bill Ackman and his wife Neri Oxman own a 5 percent stake in the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange [c23]. Ackman said Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich should not serve in Israel's next government [c22]. He said they cause reputational damage [c22]. Ben-Gvir's Jewish Power party is projected to win around 10 seats in the Israeli parliament [c25]. Smotrich's Religious Zionism is projected to win 8 seats [c25].

vocab.meaning: having the right to do or obtain something
a temporary alliance of political parties

stories.headline: Aleksandar Vučić concedes defeat as Student List wins Serbia parliamentary election
stories.body:
Serbian leader Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat in his country's parliamentary election [c27]. He has dominated Serbian politics as prime minister or president since 2014 [c32]. Last month, Vučić resigned from the presidency to trigger snap parliamentary elections [c31].

Vučić said the Student List won between 135 and 140 seats [c27]. He said his own party won 105 seats [c27]. A poll sample by CeSID-IPSPS projected the Student List would secure 138 seats [c28]. The same poll projected the Serbian Progressive Party would take 104 seats [c28]. Cardiology doctor Ilija Srdanović led 250 candidates for the Student List [c34]. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen congratulated the Student List on its victory [c33].

The collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad killed 16 people in November 2024 [c30]. That event sparked nationwide student-led protests [c30]. Voter turnout reached 64.9% by 18:00 local time [c37]. Turnout reached 67.6% by 7pm local time, marking the highest level since 1992 [c29].

Vučić blamed independent media, unnamed European nations, and an American deep state for his defeat [c35]. Election monitors reported suspected voting irregularities [c36]. These included ballot photographing and attempted vote-buying [c36]. Serbian riot police cordoned off the election commission headquarters in central Belgrade on election day [c38].

vocab.meaning: admitted defeat in a contest or election
actions that do not follow official rules or laws

stories.headline: María Corina Machado returns to Venezuela after months in exile
stories.body:
Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned home on Sunday [c39]. She had spent more than 10 months in exile [c39]. Machado is 59 years old [c47]. She fled Venezuela secretly on a speedboat in December 2025 to receive the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway [c40]. Her movement, Vente Venezuela, launched an app to collect voter registration data from Venezuelans living abroad [c46].

Machado returned by taking a private plane from Panama to Colombia and crossing overland [c44]. Supporters greeted her during a church service in Barquisimeto in Lara state [c50]. She called for new presidential elections to be held by July 2027 [c49].

US forces seized President Nicolás Maduro in January 2026 [c41]. Maduro is jailed in New York on drug, weapon, and torture charges [c41]. The Trump administration backed Delcy Rodríguez as interim president after Maduro was captured [c42]. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said US-supported reconciliation talks allowed Machado's safe return [c43].

US President Donald Trump said he knew nothing about her return [c45]. He added that the US is doing well in Venezuela [c45]. Trump had announced an oil deal with Venezuela in August 2026 [c48]. He called it the biggest oil deal in world history [c48].

vocab.meaning: the state of being barred from one's native country
the restoration of friendly relations

stories.headline: Marine Le Pen launches campaign in Orléans amid widespread French protests
stories.body:
Marine Le Pen launched her French presidential campaign on Sunday [c51]. She spoke before 8,500 supporters in Orléans [c51]. Around 3,000 police officers were deployed in Orléans ahead of her rally to prevent anti-far-right unrest [c53]. Around 13,000 people attended a peaceful counter-rally against her National Rally party in Orléans on Saturday [c64].

Her campaign launch occurred as cost-of-living and school condition protests swept France [c61]. Trade unions estimated 800,000 people participated in Saturday's protests [c61]. France's Ministry of the Interior reported that 410,000 people demonstrated nationwide on Saturday [c57]. That number included 110,000 demonstrators in Paris [c57].

Authorities deployed over 70,000 police officers and gendarmes nationwide for Saturday's demonstrations [c58]. More than 1,300 arrests were made on Saturday [c60]. More than 2,000 people were arrested across France on October 17 [c52]. The Interior Ministry reported 53 police officers were injured in clashes on Saturday [c62]. In Toulouse, a 20-year-old protester had several fingers severed when an explosive went off near him [c63].

The French Senate will debate a proposed law to make vandals pay for property damage [c54]. Le Pen said vandals will spend their whole life paying [c55]. Leftist lawmaker Éric Coquerel warned the law would end street demonstrations [c56]. Cultural institutions including the Louvre closed or cancelled events on Saturday [c59].

vocab.meaning: moved into position for military or police action
people taking part in a public protest

stories.headline: US midterm election ad spending passes ten billion dollars as Trump and Obama rally voters
stories.body:
Donald Trump attacked Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed during the US midterm campaign [c65]. El-Sayed is competing against Republican Mike Rogers for a US Senate seat in Michigan [c66]. Trump called El-Sayed a Jihadist Member of the Muslim Brotherhood on Truth Social [c70]. He alleged El-Sayed wants to impose Sharia law [c70]. Trump also claimed at a Port Huron rally that El-Sayed's mother worked for an organization that funded Osama bin Laden and Al-Qaeda [c71].

At a Michigan rally, Trump encouraged crowd members to compliment rapper Nicki Minaj's appearance [c67]. Trump also claimed the US-Canada trade war would end soon because Canada is willing to give anything [c69].

Former President Barack Obama campaigned in Detroit alongside El-Sayed and Jocelyn Benson [c72]. Obama joked that Trump has the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory [c68]. At an Ohio rally, Obama said Americans face higher living costs due to an unnecessary war [c73].

Political ad spending for the 2026 US midterm election cycle has surpassed $10 billion [c74]. Spending is projected to reach $11.6 billion [c74]. Elon Musk donated $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund [c77]. He also donated $10 million to Lone Star Liberty PAC [c77].

vocab.meaning: exceeded or gone beyond a specified amount
force something to be accepted or put in place

stories.headline: Bay of Bengal deep depression threatens Andhra Pradesh and Odisha with heavy rains
stories.body:
A weather system over the Bay of Bengal intensified into a deep depression on Saturday [c81]. The system was centered about 870 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam at 11:30 a.m. on October 25, 2026 [c81]. Forecasters expect the system to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam [c82]. It is forecast to cross as a very severe cyclonic storm by the forenoon of October 28, 2026 [c82]. The cyclone is expected to bring maximum sustained wind speeds of 115 to 125 kmph [c82]. Wind gusts could reach 140 kmph [c82].

Heavy rain forecasts cover several regions in India [c80]. Extremely heavy rainfall is forecast over Coastal Andhra Pradesh on October 27 and 28 [c80]. Heavy rain is also forecast for Odisha and Telangana on October 28 [c80]. Chhattisgarh is forecast to receive extremely heavy rainfall on October 28 and 29 [c80].

In Mankulam in Idukki, heavy weather caused a tree to fall on two cardamom plantation workers [c83]. Both workers were killed in the incident [c83].

State governments have taken emergency measures [c84]. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu ordered a high alert [c84]. He prepared 10 National Disaster Response Force teams and 11 State Disaster Response Force teams for relief operations [c84]. Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Corporation Limited cancelled employee leaves [c90]. The power company established district control rooms to handle cyclone damage [c90]. District administrations in Visakhapatnam, Anakapalli, and Alluri Sitharama Raju set up 24-hour control rooms [c91]. They also prepped relief centres [c91].

The Odisha government cancelled leaves for district collectors, district magistrates, and critical officers [c85]. Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi said that the government's primary objective is ensuring zero casualties [c89]. Majhi ordered all schools, colleges, and Anganwadi centres closed in five districts on October 28 and 29 [c86]. Those districts are Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, and Malkangiri [c86]. Odisha deployed or placed on high alert 60 ODRAF teams, 17 NDRF teams, and 225 Fire Services teams ahead of the storm [c87].

Cyclone warning signals were hoisted at nine ports [c88]. These ports include Chennai, Nagapattinam, Cuddalore, Karaikal, Pamban, and Thoothukudi [c88].

vocab.meaning: became stronger or more extreme
moving people from a place of danger to safety

stories.headline: BJP announces nationwide protests following Mallikarjun Kharge's comment about PM Modi
stories.body:
The Bharatiya Janata Party announced nationwide protests for October 26, 2026 [c92]. The protests target Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge [c92]. Kharge made remarks directed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi's late father [c92].

The incident occurred during an event in Patna marking the 139th birth anniversary of Bihar's first chief minister Shri Krishna Sinha [c94]. An audience member shouted at Kharge during the event [c94]. The audience member shouted that Modi will not go [c94]. Kharge responded to the heckler by saying that Modi's father will also go [c95].

Union Home Minister Amit Shah spoke out against the remarks [c93]. Shah said Kharge tore apart all norms of decorum with his comment in Patna [c93]. Shah claimed that repeated electoral losses over the past 12 years have driven the Congress party to desperation [c97]. He added that desperation has led Congress to the politics of slander [c97]. The BJP released a statement accusing Congress of using language associated with thugs [c98]. The statement accused Congress of functioning like a mafia gang [c98].

BJP leader Nitin Nabin criticized opposition speech [c99]. Nabin said dragging departed family members into public speeches has become standard political culture under Rahul Gandhi [c99]. Kharge called ongoing opposition protests against electoral roll revisions the second war for independence [c96].

vocab.meaning: behavior that is polite and socially acceptable
making false spoken statements damaging to a person's reputation

stories.headline: PM Modi opens RBI cybersecurity centre in Odisha and warns of banking cyber threats
stories.body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated a new data centre for the Reserve Bank of India in Bhubaneswar, Odisha [c100]. He also inaugurated a Cybersecurity Training Institute at the site [c100]. The facility was constructed at a cost of 169 crore rupees [c108]. It spans 18.55 acres at Info Valley-II in Jatni [c108]. The data centre features Tier IV accreditation across four independent facilities [c102]. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said the facility will host mission-critical systems [c106]. Those systems include RTGS and NEFT payment rails [c106].

During the event, Modi warned about cybersecurity threats [c103]. He said modern wars are fought by attacking national economies [c103]. He stressed the need to shield India's banking system from cyber terrorists [c103]. Modi also accused past Congress governments of practicing phone banking [c107]. He said past governments gave bank loans based on phone recommendations [c107].

RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra spoke at the inauguration [c101]. Malhotra said information technology is now a core function of the central bank [c101].

Modi provided figures on banking programs [c104]. He said that nearly 600 million Jan Dhan bank accounts have been opened [c104]. He added that 130 million individuals have become first-time entrepreneurs under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana [c105]. Approximately 2,100 police personnel were deployed to secure Bhubaneswar during Modi's visit [c109].

vocab.meaning: officially opened or introduced a new facility
official recognition that an establishment meets required standards
